What is probably one of the best UFO landing stories
took place in Socorro, New Mexico, in the early evening of April 24, 1964.
The trollman Lonnie Zamora said he spotted an egg-shaped object on the desert about a
mile south of Socorro.
Upon closer investigation, the object was standing on four stilt-like legs, and he could
see two human figures in white coveralls, each about four feet tall, standing near the
contrivance.
There was also a strange insignia on the side of the object, a red inverted V with bars through it.
When Zamora got to within 100 yards of the machine, it flew away narrowly missing a dynamite shack by two feet.
Police Sergeant Sam Chavez joined Zamora in a search, and they found four depressions in the soil and a rock that was grazed.
A bush close by was supposedly burned by exhaust from the saucer.
Army Captain Richard Holder checked both White Sands Missile Proving Grounds and nearby Holloman
Air Force Base, but neither used any object comparable to Zamora's machine.
J. Allen Hynek, Special UFO Consultant to the Air Force said, it is one of the soundest,
best substantiated reports as far as it goes.
One of the odd things concerning this incident is that no radar contact was made with the object.
Could it be that some of these UFOs are using an anti-radar screen,
thereby foiling our attempts to get visual evidence of their visitations?
Or was this machine really a top-secret Air Force invention?
Perhaps we'll never know for sure.

Have UFOs ever been tracked on radar or other instruments that keep track of every body in space?
The answer is yes.
In July 1965, Argentine and Chilean technicians at separate Antarctic bases photographed and observed a reddish lens-shaped UFO.
Strong interference was noted on meters and tapes.
Radio interference prevented communications with the other bases.
Later the same month, a luminous disk was sighted over the Azores,
and at this precise moment, the Weather Bureau clock stopped functioning.
In December 1964, Navy radar operators at Patuxent Naval Air Station, Maryland,
tracked two UFOs traveling at a speed of 4,800 miles per hour.
The objects were executing a right-angle turn and disappeared from the scope.
In August 1965, radar equipment at the Wichita, Kansas Weather Bureau
and Tinker Air Force Base in Oklahoma
tracked four or five objects at an altitude of 22,000 feet.
This occurred when visual sightings were being reported all over the Midwest states.

an orange-colored saucer was clocked at 90 miles an hour
